content.h1: Best IVF Treatment in Kolkata: High Success Rates & Transparent Costs
content.intro: Struggling to conceive? You are not alone — and you do not have to face this journey alone either. At Maatritva Fertility IVF & Healthcare in Newtown, Kolkata, Gold Medalist Dr. Ankita Mandal and her team have helped thousands of couples achieve their dream of parenthood using India's most advanced assisted reproductive technology.
content.whatIs: In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF) is a multi-step assisted reproductive procedure where mature eggs are retrieved from a woman's ovaries and fertilised by sperm in a state-of-the-art embryology laboratory. The resulting embryos are grown for 3–5 days, and the strongest blastocyst is transferred into the uterus to achieve pregnancy. At Maatritva IVF, we use time-lapse embryo monitoring, blastocyst culture, and personalised stimulation protocols to maximise your success.
content.whoNeedsThis: IVF is recommended for couples with blocked or damaged fallopian tubes, unexplained infertility after 12 months of trying, severe male factor infertility (low count or motility), endometriosis affecting fertility, poor ovarian reserve or low AMH, prior failed IUI cycles, and women over 38 years of age wanting to preserve conception options.
process: Step 1: Fertility Assessment — Blood work (AMH, FSH, LH), antral follicle count scan, semen analysis for both partners
Step 2: Ovarian Stimulation — 10–14 days of hormonal injections, monitored through serial ultrasounds
Step 3: Egg Retrieval — Minimally invasive, ultrasound-guided under IV sedation (15–20 minutes)
Step 4: Fertilisation & Embryo Culture — Eggs fertilised in lab, embryos grown to Day 5 blastocyst stage
Step 5: Embryo Transfer — Single best embryo placed gently into uterus (painless, no anaesthesia needed)
Step 6: Pregnancy Confirmation — Beta-hCG blood test 14 days post-transfer

faqs.question: What is the IVF success rate at Maatritva IVF Kolkata?
faqs.answer: Our IVF success rates consistently range between 65–75% for women under 35. Success depends on age, ovarian reserve, embryo quality, and underlying diagnosis. Dr. Ankita Mandal personally reviews each case to set realistic expectations.

faqs.question: What does one IVF cycle cost in Kolkata?
faqs.answer: A complete IVF cycle at Maatritva IVF costs between ₹1,20,000 and ₹2,50,000, which includes stimulation medications, monitoring, egg retrieval, embryology, and embryo transfer. We provide full cost transparency upfront — no hidden charges.

faqs.question: Is IVF painful?
faqs.answer: Injections during stimulation may cause mild discomfort. Egg retrieval is performed under short IV sedation — you will feel no pain during the procedure itself. Most patients experience only mild bloating or cramping for 1–2 days afterward.

faqs.question: How many IVF cycles will I need?
faqs.answer: Many patients conceive in 1–2 cycles. However, cumulative success increases with each attempt. Dr. Ankita discusses your personalised prognosis during the initial consultation.

faqs.question: Can women with low AMH do IVF?
faqs.answer: Yes. Low AMH means fewer eggs but quality matters more than quantity. Dr. Ankita uses customised stimulation protocols for low AMH patients, and many achieve successful pregnancies with tailored IVF.

title: ICSI Treatment in Kolkata

content.h1: ICSI Treatment in Kolkata — Precision Fertility Care for Male Factor Infertility
content.intro: When sperm quality or count makes natural fertilisation unlikely, ICSI (Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection) delivers precision results. At Maatritva IVF in Newtown, Kolkata, our expert embryologists use micromanipulation technology to inject a single healthy sperm directly into each mature egg — bypassing every natural barrier to fertilisation.
content.whatIs: ICSI is an advanced form of IVF where a single carefully selected sperm is injected directly into the cytoplasm of a mature egg using a fine glass needle under a high-powered microscope. This technique achieves fertilisation rates of 70–80% even in cases of severely compromised sperm. It is particularly effective when combined with surgical sperm retrieval (TESA/PESA) for men with azoospermia.
content.whoNeedsThis: ICSI is indicated for severe male factor infertility (count below 5 million, motility below 10%, or total motility below 1%), previous IVF cycles with poor or zero fertilisation, surgically retrieved sperm (TESA, PESA, micro-TESE), frozen sperm with limited quantity, and cases of unexplained fertilisation failure.
process: Step 1: Simultaneous partner evaluations — semen analysis with DNA fragmentation + female hormonal panel
Step 2: Ovarian stimulation and monitoring (same as IVF)
Step 3: Egg retrieval under sedation
Step 4: Sperm selection under 400x magnification by embryologist
Step 5: Microinjection — single sperm injected into each mature egg
Step 6: Embryo culture to blastocyst stage; best embryo transferred on Day 5

faqs.question: How is ICSI different from standard IVF?
faqs.answer: In standard IVF, thousands of sperm are placed with each egg and fertilisation happens naturally. In ICSI, a single sperm is injected directly into the egg — essential when sperm quality is too low for natural fertilisation.

faqs.question: My husband's sperm count is nearly zero — can ICSI still help?
faqs.answer: Yes. With surgical sperm retrieval techniques like TESA or micro-TESE combined with ICSI, even men with azoospermia (zero sperm in ejaculate) can father biological children. Maatritva IVF has helped many such couples.

faqs.question: Are ICSI babies healthy?
faqs.answer: Yes. Over 30 years of global data confirm ICSI babies develop completely normally with no increased risk of birth defects compared to naturally conceived children.

content.h1: IUI Treatment in Kolkata — A Gentle, Affordable First Step to Parenthood
content.intro: For many couples, Intrauterine Insemination (IUI) is the perfect starting point in the fertility journey — less invasive, significantly more affordable than IVF, and highly effective for the right candidates. At Maatritva IVF, Newtown, Dr. Ankita Mandal carefully selects and times each IUI cycle for maximum impact.
content.whatIs: IUI involves placing a concentrated, laboratory-washed sample of the most motile sperm directly into the uterine cavity through a thin catheter at the precise time of ovulation. By bypassing the cervix and dramatically increasing the concentration of healthy sperm near the fallopian tubes, IUI significantly improves the chance of natural fertilisation. The procedure takes just 5–10 minutes and requires no anaesthesia.
content.whoNeedsThis: IUI is recommended for couples with unexplained infertility under 35 years old, mild male factor infertility (slightly low count or motility), cervical mucus hostility, single women or same-sex couples using donor sperm, and patients who prefer a less invasive, lower-cost initial approach before considering IVF.
process: Step 1: Baseline blood work and ultrasound on Day 2–3 of cycle
Step 2: Ovulation induction with oral medications (Letrozole/Clomiphene) or low-dose injections
Step 3: Serial ultrasound monitoring to track follicle growth
Step 4: Trigger injection when follicle reaches 18–22mm
Step 5: Semen collection and laboratory washing/concentration
Step 6: Catheter-guided sperm placement into uterus (5–10 minutes, no anaesthesia)

faqs.question: How many IUI cycles should we try before moving to IVF?
faqs.answer: Dr. Ankita typically recommends 3–4 well-timed IUI cycles. If pregnancy has not occurred by then, she will discuss whether IVF or other approaches are more appropriate based on your specific situation and age.

faqs.question: Does IUI hurt?
faqs.answer: IUI is virtually painless — most women compare it to a routine Pap smear. No anaesthesia is needed. Some experience very mild cramping for a few hours afterward.

faqs.question: What is the cost of IUI in Kolkata?
faqs.answer: At Maatritva IVF, a complete IUI cycle including monitoring costs between ₹8,000–₹20,000 depending on whether medications and tracking scans are included.

content.h1: Egg Freezing in Kolkata — Preserve Your Fertility, On Your Own Timeline
content.intro: Whether you're focused on your career, awaiting the right partner, or facing a medical condition that threatens ovarian function, egg freezing gives you the freedom to plan motherhood on your terms. At Maatritva IVF in Newtown, we use vitrification — the gold-standard ultra-rapid flash-freezing technique — with egg survival rates exceeding 90%.
content.whatIs: Egg freezing (oocyte cryopreservation) involves stimulating the ovaries to produce multiple mature eggs, retrieving them under a brief procedure, and immediately preserving them at -196°C in liquid nitrogen using vitrification. These eggs can remain viable indefinitely and are used for IVF when you decide to start your family — fertilised with sperm via ICSI, grown into embryos, and transferred.
content.whoNeedsThis: Egg freezing is ideal for women aged 25–38 who wish to delay motherhood for career, personal, or relationship reasons; women about to undergo chemotherapy or pelvic radiation; those with endometriosis, autoimmune disorders, or a family history of early menopause; and anyone who wants reproductive insurance before age-related decline.
process: Step 1: Fertility assessment — AMH test, antral follicle count scan, hormonal panel
Step 2: Personalised ovarian stimulation protocol (10–12 days of self-injected hormones)
Step 3: Daily monitoring via serial ultrasounds to track egg development
Step 4: Egg trigger injection when follicles are mature (≥18mm)
Step 5: Egg retrieval under short IV sedation (15–20 minutes)
Step 6: Vitrification — eggs flash-frozen at -196°C within minutes of retrieval

faqs.question: What is the best age to freeze eggs?
faqs.answer: The ideal window is before age 35. Egg quality and quantity decline after 35, particularly sharply after 37. However, women in their early 40s can still benefit. Dr. Ankita assesses your individual ovarian reserve to advise personally.

faqs.question: How long can frozen eggs be stored?
faqs.answer: Vitrified eggs can be stored indefinitely in liquid nitrogen without deterioration. Healthy babies have been born from eggs frozen for over 10 years. Annual storage fees apply after the first year.

faqs.question: How many eggs should I freeze?
faqs.answer: As a general guide, 15–20 mature eggs give a strong chance of at least one future live birth. Older patients or those with lower reserves may need multiple retrieval cycles. Dr. Ankita provides personalised guidance based on your AMH and AFC.

content.h1: Donor Egg IVF in Kolkata — Your Best Chance at Motherhood
content.intro: When your own eggs cannot achieve pregnancy — due to age, premature ovarian failure, or repeated IVF failure — donor egg IVF offers the highest success rates in assisted reproduction. At Maatritva IVF in Newtown, our ICMR-compliant donor programme is built on ethical screening, compassionate matching, and exceptional clinical outcomes.
content.whatIs: Donor egg IVF uses eggs from a rigorously screened, young, healthy donor. These eggs are fertilised with the male partner's sperm via IVF/ICSI in our laboratory, and the resulting embryos are transferred into the recipient mother's prepared uterus. Because donor eggs come from young women with optimal egg quality, success rates often exceed 55–65% per cycle — significantly higher than standard IVF with own eggs for women over 40.
content.whoNeedsThis: Donor egg IVF is recommended for women with premature ovarian failure or very low ovarian reserve, women over 40–42 with repeated IVF failure using own eggs, those with genetic conditions they wish to avoid passing on, women who have had bilateral oophorectomy, and cases of repeated poor egg quality despite optimal stimulation protocols.

Step 2: Donor matching based on physical characteristics, blood group, and health history
Step 3: Donor undergoes comprehensive medical, genetic, hormonal, and psychological screening
Step 4: Donor ovarian stimulation and egg retrieval
Step 5: Recipient uterus preparation with hormonal medications
Step 6: Fertilisation of donor eggs with partner's sperm, embryo culture, and transfer

faqs.question: Will the baby look like me if I use donor eggs?
faqs.answer: Donors are carefully matched on physical traits including complexion, height, build, and blood group. Recent epigenetics research shows the recipient mother's uterine environment actively influences gene expression in the growing baby.

faqs.question: Is donor egg IVF legal in India?
faqs.answer: Yes. Donor egg IVF is fully legal and regulated by the ICMR and the ART Regulation Act 2021. At Maatritva IVF, we follow all guidelines strictly. All donations are anonymous and confidential.

faqs.question: What is the donor egg IVF success rate?
faqs.answer: Our donor egg IVF programme achieves 55–65% clinical pregnancy rates per cycle. Since egg quality from young donors is optimal, age of the recipient is less critical — making it one of the best options for older women.

content.h1: Laparoscopic Surgery for Infertility in Kolkata — Keyhole Precision, Maximum Results
content.intro: Many women struggling to conceive have an underlying structural cause that can only be identified and corrected through surgery. At Maatritva IVF, Dr. Ankita Mandal performs advanced laparoscopic (keyhole) surgery to diagnose and treat conditions like blocked fallopian tubes, endometriosis, ovarian cysts, and uterine fibroids — often restoring natural fertility or dramatically improving IVF success rates.
content.whatIs: Laparoscopic surgery uses a tiny camera (laparoscope) and miniature instruments inserted through 2–3 small abdominal cuts (5–10mm each). This allows Dr. Ankita to examine the pelvic organs in real-time and treat abnormalities in the same session. Compared to open surgery, recovery is 3–4 times faster with significantly less pain, scarring, and hospital time.
content.whoNeedsThis: Laparoscopic surgery for infertility is indicated for women with blocked or damaged fallopian tubes (hydrosalpinx), endometriosis (stages 1–4), ovarian cysts or endometriomas affecting egg quality, uterine fibroids distorting the cavity, adhesions from previous infections or surgeries, and unexplained infertility where pelvic factor needs investigation.
process: Step 1: Pre-operative assessment — blood work, imaging, anaesthesia fitness check
Step 2: Dr. Ankita explains the procedure, answers questions, and obtains consent
Step 3: General anaesthesia is administered; 2–3 small incisions made (5–10mm)
Step 4: Pelvic cavity inspected with laparoscope — tubes, ovaries, uterus examined
Step 5: Any abnormalities (adhesions, cysts, fibroids, endometriosis) treated in the same session
Step 6: Incisions closed; most patients go home the same day or next morning

faqs.question: When can I try to conceive after laparoscopic surgery?
faqs.answer: Most women can resume trying within 1–2 months after surgery. For conditions like adhesiolysis or endometriosis treatment, natural conception rates improve significantly in the first 6–12 months post-surgery.

faqs.question: Will I have visible scars?
faqs.answer: Laparoscopic incisions are tiny — just 5–10mm. They fade over a few months and become nearly invisible. This is one of the key advantages over traditional open surgery.

faqs.question: Should I do laparoscopy before IVF?
faqs.answer: For some conditions like hydrosalpinx (fluid-filled blocked tubes) or large endometriomas, surgery before IVF can actually improve IVF success rates significantly. Dr. Ankita individually evaluates whether surgery or direct IVF is the better path for you.

content.whatIs: Fertility preservation refers to freezing eggs, sperm, or embryos before medical treatment (chemotherapy, radiation, surgery) that may damage reproductive function. Using our vitrification cryo-bank with liquid nitrogen storage at -196°C, preserved gametes remain viable indefinitely — ready to use for IVF/ICSI whenever you are ready to start your family after completing treatment.
content.whoNeedsThis: Fertility preservation is critical for cancer patients about to begin chemotherapy or pelvic radiation, women requiring ovarian surgery that reduces egg reserve, patients receiving gonadotoxic therapy for autoimmune conditions like Lupus, transgender individuals before hormone therapy, and anyone who wishes to protect fertility before medical treatment.
process: Step 1: Urgent referral consultation — Dr. Ankita coordinates with your oncologist within 24–48 hours

Step 4: 10–14 days of stimulation with daily monitoring
Step 5: Egg retrieval and immediate vitrification; sperm collected separately
Step 6: Secure long-term storage; when ready for family, IVF/ICSI initiated with stored samples

faqs.question: How quickly can we start fertility preservation?
faqs.answer: We can initiate within 2–3 days of your first consultation. Random-start stimulation protocols mean you do not need to wait for a specific time in your menstrual cycle. Time is critical and we treat it as such.

faqs.question: Will egg freezing delay my cancer treatment?
faqs.answer: In most cases, egg freezing takes 10–14 days and does not significantly delay cancer treatment start. We coordinate closely with your oncologist to ensure both fertility and cancer care timelines are respected.

content.h1: TESA & PESA in Kolkata — Surgical Sperm Retrieval for Azoospermia
content.intro: Zero sperm in the ejaculate does not mean zero hope. TESA (Testicular Sperm Extraction) and PESA (Percutaneous Epididymal Sperm Aspiration) are minimally invasive surgical procedures that retrieve sperm directly from the testes or epididymis. Combined with ICSI at Maatritva IVF in Newtown, these techniques have helped many men with azoospermia father biological children.
content.whatIs: TESA involves inserting a fine needle into the testis under local anaesthesia to aspirate sperm-containing tissue. PESA aspirates sperm from the epididymis — the coiled structure behind the testes — and is used for obstructive azoospermia. For non-obstructive azoospermia (where sperm production is impaired), micro-TESE uses a microscope to find the tiny pockets of active sperm production within the testes — offering the highest retrieval rate available.
content.whoNeedsThis: TESA/PESA is recommended for men with obstructive azoospermia (blocked vas deferens, post-vasectomy), non-obstructive azoospermia (Sertoli cell only, hypospermia), ejaculatory dysfunction, failed vasectomy reversal, and any case where sperm cannot be obtained through ejaculation.
process: Step 1: Comprehensive evaluation — FSH, LH, testosterone, karyotype, Y-chromosome microdeletion testing
Step 2: Procedure selection — TESA, PESA, or micro-TESE based on diagnosis
Step 3: Procedure under local anaesthesia or short IV sedation
Step 4: Embryologist immediately examines retrieved tissue for viable sperm
Step 5: Sperm used directly for ICSI or cryopreserved for future cycles
Step 6: Post-operative rest 2–3 days; partner's IVF cycle coordinated simultaneously

faqs.question: Is TESA painful?
faqs.answer: TESA is performed under local anaesthesia with sedation. You may feel slight pressure but no significant pain. Mild soreness for 2–3 days afterward is managed with standard painkillers.

faqs.question: What if no sperm are found?
faqs.answer: While possible in non-obstructive azoospermia, micro-TESE maximises the chance of finding sperm even in small pockets. If no sperm are found, Dr. Ankita will compassionately discuss donor sperm options.

content.h1: Hysteroscopy in Kolkata — See Inside, Diagnose & Treat in One Sitting
content.intro: Many women undergo multiple failed IVF cycles without ever knowing the inside of their uterus is the hidden obstacle. A single hysteroscopy can identify and fix uterine polyps, fibroids, adhesions, or a septum — dramatically improving both natural conception and IVF implantation rates. At Maatritva IVF, Dr. Ankita Mandal performs both diagnostic and operative hysteroscopy as a critical component of the fertility workup.
content.whatIs: Hysteroscopy involves inserting a thin, lighted telescope (hysteroscope) through the cervix to directly visualise the uterine cavity in real-time on a monitor. It is the gold standard for diagnosing intrauterine abnormalities that ultrasound often misses. Operative hysteroscopy allows simultaneous treatment — removing polyps, dividing a septum, or releasing adhesions — in one sitting.
content.whoNeedsThis: Hysteroscopy is recommended before IVF for women with unexplained infertility where uterine factors are suspected, recurrent implantation failure, recurrent miscarriage (2+), abnormal uterine bleeding, suspected polyps or fibroids on ultrasound, and those being evaluated for uterine anatomical issues.
process: Step 1: Baseline ultrasound review and pre-procedure blood work
Step 2: Procedure scheduled in first half of menstrual cycle for optimal visibility
Step 3: Hysteroscope inserted gently through cervix; uterine cavity filled with saline for visualization
Step 4: Entire cavity examined — fundus, orifices, endometrium
Step 5: Any polyps, adhesions, septum removed during same session using operative instruments
Step 6: Patient recovers for 1–2 hours and goes home; fertility treatment resumes next cycle

faqs.question: Is hysteroscopy painful?
faqs.answer: Diagnostic hysteroscopy causes minimal discomfort — comparable to a Pap smear. Operative procedures may use short anaesthesia. Most women experience only mild cramping afterward.

faqs.question: Should I do hysteroscopy before every IVF cycle?
faqs.answer: Dr. Ankita recommends a hysteroscopy before the first IVF cycle to ensure the uterine cavity is clear. Studies show it can improve IVF success rates by up to 50% by identifying and correcting missed abnormalities.

content.h1: High-Risk Pregnancy Management in Kolkata — Expert Care, Complete Peace of Mind
content.intro: Every pregnancy is precious — but some require a closer, more expert eye. Dr. Ankita Mandal at Maatritva IVF in Newtown, Kolkata has extensive experience managing complex, high-risk pregnancies, from IVF-conceived twins to advanced maternal age and gestational diabetes. Her approach combines cutting-edge fetal monitoring with genuine emotional support, so you can focus entirely on welcoming your baby.
content.whatIs: A high-risk pregnancy is one where the mother, baby, or both face increased health complications compared to a standard pregnancy. These include IVF/ICSI pregnancies (which require closer early monitoring), multiples (twins or triplets), advanced maternal age (35+), pre-existing medical conditions (diabetes, hypertension, thyroid disorders), previous complicated deliveries, or conditions like placenta praevia or preeclampsia developing during pregnancy.
content.whoNeedsThis: High-risk pregnancy care is essential for IVF or ICSI pregnancies, multiple pregnancies (twins, triplets), women over 35, those with pre-existing diabetes, hypertension, autoimmune or thyroid conditions, a history of recurrent pregnancy loss or preterm birth, and pregnancies with detected fetal anomalies requiring ongoing monitoring.
process: Step 1: Comprehensive early assessment — full blood panel, baseline kidney and liver function, early anomaly scan
Step 2: Personalised monitoring schedule based on your specific risk factors
Step 3: More frequent ultrasounds — growth scans, Doppler studies every 2–3 weeks from 24 weeks
Step 4: Maternal monitoring — blood pressure, blood sugar, thyroid, urine protein checks
Step 5: Detailed birth plan discussion from 32 weeks, coordinating with neonatology if required
Step 6: Post-delivery follow-up and planning for future pregnancies

faqs.question: Is an IVF pregnancy automatically high-risk?
faqs.answer: IVF pregnancies are monitored more closely in the early weeks but many progress just like natural pregnancies. The label ensures you receive extra care — it does not mean something will go wrong.

faqs.question: I am 40 and pregnant. Should I be worried?
faqs.answer: Many women in their 40s have perfectly healthy pregnancies. Advanced maternal age does warrant additional screening, but with proper care from Dr. Ankita, outcomes are excellent.
